title: Applying for a Schengen visa for the Netherlands in Serbia

embassy_in_serbia.name: Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands in Belgrade

visa_eligibility.serbian_citizens: Serbian citizens require a Schengen visa to visit the Netherlands for stays up to 90 days. They must apply at the Embassy of the Netherlands in Belgrade if they reside in Serbia.
visa_eligibility.other_nationals: Any foreign national residing in Serbia may apply at the Belgrade embassy. Applicants can only submit their application at the embassy in the country where they legally reside.

processing_times.recommended_submission_weeks_before_trav: 6–12 weeks (apply up to 6 months ahead, no later than 45 days before travel)
processing_times.notes: Standard processing is 15 calendar days. Processing can extend to 45 days if there is a spike in applications. Apply no later than 45 days before your trip; you may apply up to 6 months in advance.

application_location.center: Embassy of the Netherlands in Belgrade
application_location.booking: Book online at the VFS appointment portal: https://www.vfsvisaonline.com/Netherlands-Global-Online-Appointment_Zone2/AppScheduling/AppWelcome.aspx?P=KWfLdX/GTmuYQUeqIQEOCNnhmBT2ceX+c/qmPvZwnLg= or by email at bel-ca@minbuza.nl. Book yourself to avoid intermediary costs. Make a separate appointment for each applicant. Personal attendance is mandatory. Passport collection (no appointment needed): Wednesday and Thursday 9:30–11:30.

visa_fees.service_fee: Fees apply even if exempt from the visa fee when applying through VFS Global or TLScontact. Payment must be made by credit or debit card; cash in euros accepted only in emergencies.
fee_exemptions: Children under 6 years old (free of charge)
Students and accompanying teachers traveling for educational purposes
Persons under 26 years old representing a non-profit organisation at sporting, cultural, educational events, or conferences
Citizens of Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus pay a reduced fee of €35

required_documents_all_applicants: Completed and signed Schengen visa application form (filled out online via official portal)
Valid passport (not more than 10 years old, at least 2 empty visa pages, valid at least 3 months after departure date, bearing your signature)
Colour photo (3.5cm × 4.5cm, white/light background, taken within the last 6 months)
Proof of legal residence in Serbia (original + colour copy): passport, residence permit, visa, or work permit valid at least 3 months after departure
Proof of ties to home country (employment letter with salary, or self-employment documentation, or student enrollment, or property ownership)
Proof of travel medical insurance covering at least €30,000 in medical expenses across all Schengen countries for the full duration of stay
Travel reservation (colour copy of outbound and return booking; a paid ticket is not required)
Proof of accommodation for entire stay (hotel reservation or rental agreement)
Financial proof showing who pays travel and stay costs (e.g., 3 months of bank statements and recent payslips if self-paying)
additional_documents_by_nationality: Citizens of Armenia, Azerbaijan, and Belarus are subject to a reduced fee of €35 under the visa facilitation agreement

required: Parental consent form signed by non-travelling parent(s) (original + colour copy)
Colour copy of travel documents of non-travelling parent(s) or guardian(s)
Court or guardianship documentation if applicable
documents_for_minors.note: All minors (under 18) must appear in person at the appointment to submit their application, even if accompanied by a parent or guardian.

tourism: Hotel reservation or rental agreement for the entire trip duration
Proof of sufficient funds (3 months bank statements + recent payslips if self-funding)
business: Invitation letter from the host organisation in the Netherlands stating applicant's personal details, visit dates, and reasons for the visit
Accommodation confirmation (hotel or stated in invitation letter)
3 months bank statements showing financial means
family_or_private_visit: Invitation letter from the host in the Netherlands
Proof of host's legal status in the Netherlands (copy of passport or residence permit)
medical_treatment: Confirmation letter from a medical institution in the Netherlands stating the nature and duration of treatment
Proof of sufficient funds to cover medical and living costs
transit: Airport transit visa (ATV) if required by nationality
Proof of onward travel (valid visa/residence permit for destination country and travel booking)

employees: Employment letter stating position, salary, and approved leave
students: Proof of financial support (scholarship letter, parental support, or bank statements)
retirees: Proof of pension income (pension statement or bank statements showing regular pension transfers)

special_provisions: The Netherlands Embassy in Belgrade is also responsible for Montenegro. Serbian citizens do not currently benefit from visa liberalisation for the Netherlands (Schengen). Applications submitted through intermediaries are strongly discouraged — applicants should book their own appointments to avoid unnecessary costs. The embassy observes Dutch and Serbian public holidays and additional closure days throughout the year.
